newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bond yields remain down after data.
newsitem.headline: Australian bond yields remain down after data.

text.p: *Australian bond yields remained lower during a relative light trading session, with a sharp fall in first quarter business inventories helping to underpin the move.
*Focus remains on Friday's April retail trade data.

Australian bond yields remained lower during a relative light trading session with a sharp fall in first quarter business inventories helping to underpin the move, although it failed to cause a marked reaction.
Stocks fell 2.1 percent against a forecast 0.5 percent rise, and analysts expect it will detract 1.7 percentage points from GDP, much larger than the 0.5 percent that had been expected.

"In the short-term, it's quite supportive, longer term its consistent with the view that the economy will have to be a little bit stronger," said Stephen Koukoulas, chief economist at Citibank Australia.
Also released were April balance of goods and services data, which showed a A$302 million surplus, higher than the forecast A$100 million, and after a A$103 million deficit in March.
Domestic bonds started the day with a modestly positive tone with the short end still finding support after last week's official rate cut, and after a flat U.S. Treasuries preformance.

"The three-year bond still has a bit of life in it, while the long end is taking its lead from overseas. And I think the three/10-year spread at around 120 basis points is about right in the current climate," said Stephen Roberts, chief economist at UBS Australia.
Analysts still see the three-year bond offering value with a spread of around 90 basis points over an official cash rate of 5.5 percent and in view of the benign inflation outlook.
However, the long end remains vulnerable to moves offshore, particularly in the U.S. with the spread between the two now around its tightest in three years, they added.
The contrast between the three and 10-year maturities has seen the futures spread blow out to just under 120 basis points from around 94 basis points a week ago.

The local market's modest bid tone saw it outpace the dollar bloc. Canadian debt underperformed again amid some foreign selling on Wednesday, linked to the approach of next week's Canadian election. The Canadian market has recently been undermined by the threat of a Fed tightening.

The three-year bond made a further retest of 93.60, the level that was seen immediately after last week's rate cut and briefly matched on Wednesday, but is still proving a stiff barrier. Key resistance is seen at 93.65, the 1997 peak.
